svg.style: background: transparent; background-color: transparent; color-scheme: light dark;

g.text: How a band is computed — two instruments, one vocabulary
Both paths end in the same four values. That is what makes a resource band comparable to a use-case band at all.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(237, 231, 246), rgb(39, 34, 46)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(94, 53, 177), rgb(197, 161, 255));

g.text: A · USE CASE — a questionnaire someone answers
Asks what could happen to a person if this goes wrong.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(94, 53, 177), rgb(197, 161, 255));
fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(94, 53, 177), rgb(197, 161, 255));
fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(94, 53, 177), rgb(197, 161, 255));
fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 248, 225), rgb(30, 24, 4)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(249, 168, 37), rgb(149, 79, 0));
fill: light-dark(rgb(251, 250, 245), rgb(23, 22, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(230, 220, 192), rgb(57, 48, 24));

g.text: The rules are not decoration. A single answer — "the user base is external" — can force three other answers to their
maximum and put a floor under the whole assessment, moving it two levels without touching the matrix.
Answered by a person — it is a business judgement the platform cannot observe.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(232, 245, 233), rgb(21, 33, 22)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(46, 125, 50), rgb(100, 168, 104));

g.text: At the promotion gate these answers arrive pre-populated from the exported use-case pack, not blank.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(245, 249, 255), rgb(21, 24, 29)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(21, 101, 192), rgb(99, 168, 246));

g.text: B · AGENT / MODEL / MCP SERVER — signals the platform observes
Asks what it can reach and what authority it holds.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(21, 101, 192), rgb(99, 168, 246));
fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(21, 101, 192), rgb(99, 168, 246));
fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(21, 101, 192), rgb(99, 168, 246));

g.text: score reads as a share of

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(21, 101, 192), rgb(99, 168, 246));
fill: light-dark(rgb(250, 250, 250), rgb(22, 22, 22)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(224, 224, 224), rgb(45, 45, 45));

g.text: Every signal here is observable without asking anyone. That is the property that lets an unregistered resource
be classified from what it is doing, rather than waiting for an owner who is not going to fill in a form.
Computed, not answered — no human in the path.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 235, 238), rgb(44, 27, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(198, 40, 40), rgb(255, 145, 145));

g.text: ONLY INHERENT SIGNALS FEED THE SCORE. Controls — registration, inbound authentication, human review,
evaluations, guardrails — are carried beside the band as mitigations, never netted off it.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 248, 225), rgb(30, 24, 4)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(249, 168, 37), rgb(149, 79, 0));

g.text: ONE BAND VOCABULARY — low · medium · high · critical
A member may keep its own level names for its committees — those stay in the record. The band is what crosses the boundary,
because a platform gate can only compare something it can rank.

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(94, 53, 177), rgb(197, 161, 255)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(94, 53, 177), rgb(197, 161, 255));
fill: light-dark(rgb(21, 101, 192), rgb(99, 168, 246)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(21, 101, 192), rgb(99, 168, 246));

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(236, 239, 241), rgb(31, 33, 35)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(96, 125, 139), rgb(114, 139, 151));

g.text: WHAT THE BAND IS THEN USED FOR

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(96, 125, 139), rgb(114, 139, 151));

g.text: Is the resource at or below its use case's band?

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(96, 125, 139), rgb(114, 139, 151));

g.text: Which obligations, approvals and evaluations apply.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(96, 125, 139), rgb(114, 139, 151));

g.text: Whether it may move to a higher environment.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(96, 125, 139), rgb(114, 139, 151));

g.text: Every band names the exact question set and thresholds
it was judged against, so a past decision still explains itself.
